tools.name: get_asset_document_schema
tools.description: Read the AssetDocument authoring guide (workflow, document header, omitted-vs-empty rule, validate and diff, results and diagnostics, compile status, sidecar files) before authoring. Without profile: the guide and the list of profile sections; with profile: that section (the profile's Body shapes, its list_types kinds and tools).

profile.description: Class path (e.g. /Script/AIModule.BehaviorTree; a class without a section gets Generic), section name (e.g. DataTable) or "all".

part.description: A reference part of the section (its last line lists them).

tools.name: find_assets
tools.description: Find assets in the Asset Registry (project, engine and plugin content) as the Content Browser filters them: package path prefix, class (subclasses included), name, and uses (what their graphs use or reference; syntax and result rows in the Blueprint section of get_asset_document_schema). Read-only, paged, sorted by path: {Total, Offset, Assets[{ObjectPath, Class}], NextOffset?}.

name.description: Case-insensitive substring, or wildcard with * and ? (e.g. BB_*).

uses.description: Terms that must all match; | separates alternatives. A term is an action key (K2:CallArrayFunction), node class, function, or asset path (assets referencing it). E.g. ["K2:PromotableOperator", "K2:CallArrayFunction|/Script/Engine.BlueprintSetLibrary"].

tools.name: list_types
tools.description: List the types the editor's pickers offer: kind class, struct or enum (classes include unloaded Blueprint classes; structs with base /Script/Engine.TableRowBase include User Defined Structs; enums include User Defined Enums), or a profile's catalog: MetaSound nodes / data types / interfaces, IK Rig solvers and retarget ops, Control Rig nodes / types / modules, Sequencer tracks / sections / bindings, Sound Cue nodes, EQS generators / tests, Blueprint actions (each profile section explains its kinds). Read-only, paged: {Total, Offset, Types[{Path, ...}], NextOffset?}. inspect_asset_document_target on a /Script struct or enum path shows its fields or values.

base.description: Only subclasses of this class or struct; blueprint_node: the Blueprint or class giving the context.

name.description: Case-insensitive substring, or wildcard with * and ? (spaces allowed).

schema.description: StateTree: only the node types this schema offers; sequencer_track: the sequence class (default LevelSequence).

graph.description: blueprint_node: a function graph of base (default its event graph).

target.description: blueprint_node: functions callable on this class (its interfaces' included), as when dragging off a pin of it.

tools.name: inspect_asset_document_target
tools.description: Inspect a class, asset or type. A class or asset: the properties a document can author (type, value, default, writability; skipped ones with the reason) and facts to build on (skeleton slots, sockets, bones; mesh Bounds in cm and MaterialSlots; an Actor Blueprint's MeshComponents with their mesh and its slots; animation length, root motion, notifies; sound duration; material parameters; compile status; row schema; profile details). A /Script struct or enum: its fields or values. Engine and plugin assets: read_only. A bare User Defined Enum / Struct name finds that asset; a path naming no asset resolves to the only asset of that name under its mount, else lists candidates. Abstract classes: Abstract: true (not a document Class).

detail.description: true: the whole. Default: summarized (payload Summary says what): large nested struct / instanced values as type and size, skipped grouped by reason.

tools.name: inspect_asset_document_profile
tools.description: Show which AssetDocument profile owns a class or asset and what it accepts: BodySections, fragment kinds, region policies (a class without an exact profile: the generic profile, Properties only). get_asset_document_schema with profile has the Body shapes.

debug.description: Also the runtime registration (runtime debugging only).

tools.name: create_asset_document_template
tools.description: Create a starting AssetDocument for an exact class path and a target path, following the class's profile (exact profiles: their Body skeleton; generic: Properties only). For an existing asset use extract_asset_document.

tools.name: extract_asset_document
tools.description: Extract an asset as its canonical AssetDocument (payload), the starting point for edits; Blueprint-family results carry compile. Engine and plugin assets extract read-only (read_only: true): for an editable copy set Target to a new /Game path (and replace the source's own path elsewhere), Action Create, and apply it, or use duplicate_asset (preferred for Blueprints).

diff_only.description: Default true: omit values equal to their defaults (applying the result is still a no-op); false lists every writable value.

tools.name: validate_asset_document
tools.description: Validate one AssetDocument (document or sidecar file_path) without changing anything: apply's checks and diagnostics; on success the message says what apply would do ('would create', 'would change N value(s)', 'would change nothing'). What it cannot check: core guide, Validate And Diff.

file_path.description: Absolute sidecar file path (instead of document).

tools.name: diff_asset_document
tools.description: Diff one AssetDocument (document or sidecar file_path) against the asset without changing it: what apply would change, as entries {path (JSON Pointer into the document), kind (Add: only the document has it; Remove: only the asset; Replace), before (asset), after (document)}. A missing asset diffs as would_create.

file_path.description: Absolute sidecar file path (instead of document).

tools.name: apply_asset_document_file
tools.description: Apply an AssetDocument sidecar file (<Content dir>/<path>/<Asset>.assetdoc.json, health_check gives contentDir; Target must match that path), written first. If the editor's file watcher already applied it, the result says applied_by: 'file_watcher'. A failed create keeps the sidecar (sidecar_kept: true). If the call returns no result (connection error, timeout), do not retry blindly: health_check, then diff_asset_document (empty: applied). Blueprint-family results carry compile.

tools.name: duplicate_asset
tools.description: Copy an asset into /Game as the Content Browser's Duplicate does, and save the copy: the editable copy of an engine or plugin asset (find_assets lists them). Only that asset is copied; the copy references what the source references. A map is copied with its actor files (payload.external_packages); a World Partition map open in the editor is refused (open another map first). Errors: Duplicate.SourceNotFound, UnsupportedSource, InvalidTarget, TargetExists.

source.description: Package or object path of any asset.

tools.name: sync_asset_document
tools.description: Sidecar mirroring (health_check sidecar_sync.enabled; the user turns it on in Project Settings): status of mirrored sidecars (no targets: counts and open issues; targets: checked now), resolve a conflict with accept_sidecar (apply the edited sidecar) or accept_asset (rewrite the sidecar from the asset), or materialize missing sidecars in the background. Errors: Sync.MirroringOff, InvalidAction, InvalidTarget.

targets.description: /Game assets (accept_*: required) or folders (status, materialize; default all of /Game).

regions.description: accept_*: JSON Pointers such as /Properties or /Body/Keys; default every conflicted region.

tools.name: sample_animation_bones
tools.description: Read where bones or sockets of an AnimSequence, AnimComposite or AnimMontage are at given times, evaluated as the editor does (read-only): Location, Rotation (and Speed) per bone and time. Options, result, limits and errors: AnimSequence section of get_asset_document_schema.

tools.name: retarget_animations
tools.description: Duplicate and retarget animations through an IK Retargeter, as its Export Selected Animations / the Content Browser's Retarget Animations does, and save the new assets. Naming, existing outputs, result and errors: IKRig section of get_asset_document_schema.

assets.description: Animation assets on the source skeleton.

tools.name: health_check
tools.description: Check that the Unreal Editor's HTTP server is running; reports its port, the project directory and contentDir (where .assetdoc.json sidecars go).

tools.name: get_editor_context
tools.description: The editor's current state: selected actors (with transform) and Content Browser assets, current level, open asset editors, PIE status and editor modes: what the user is working on. pendingNotices lists problems from work the editor did on its own that are still open, e.g. a sidecar the file watcher applied and that failed (file, code, message); a tool result also reports a new one once.

tools.name: query_level
tools.description: Read the level open in the editor (read-only). what "world": the summary (levels, World Partition, folders, layers, actor counts, dirty_packages). Default: actors, filtered and paged, each with its path (the stable reference), guid, label, class, level, folder, tags, transform; detail components / properties (= full) add more; properties reads value paths into values. Refused during Play In Editor (query_play reads the game). Fields: get_level_editing_guide (read it first).

name.description: Wildcard over label and object name.

tools.name: edit_level
tools.description: Edit the level open in the editor: a batch of ops (spawn, duplicate, set, delete, components, attachment, folders, World Partition pins) applied as ONE transaction, i.e. one Edit > Undo entry titled by description. Everything is checked before anything changes; a failure rolls the whole batch back (rolled_back: true). dry_run: true checks and describes only. Actors by path (query_level) or "@id" of an earlier spawn / duplicate; values in AssetDocument value forms. Not saved unless save: true. Refused during Play In Editor. Op fields: get_level_editing_guide (read it first).

description.description: Undo entry title, e.g. "AI: build lit room".

save.description: Save the packages this batch dirtied.

tools.name: undo_editor
tools.description: Edit > Undo (or Redo) of one entry a result of yours named: edit_level transaction.title / id, execute_python undo_title / undo_id. Only that entry: when the newest entry is another one (e.g. the user's edit), nothing changes and the result is Undo.EntryMismatch naming it. Result: the entry, can_undo, can_redo, next_undo, next_redo. Refused during Play In Editor.

tools.name: open_level
tools.description: File > Open Level: open the map at path. Unsaved changes of the open level are never discarded: refused (Level.UnsavedChangesWouldBeLost, listing them) unless save_first: true saves them first. Clears the Undo history; returns the world summary. Refused during Play In Editor.

tools.name: new_level
tools.description: File > New Level: create a map from a template ("empty" default, "empty_open_world", "basic", "open_world"), save it at path and open it. Unsaved changes as open_level; Level.MapExists when path is taken.

tools.name: get_level_editing_guide
tools.description: Read a guide for the editor tools (not asset documents). Default topic "level": query_level, edit_level, undo_editor, open_level / new_level and the Level.* codes. "playtest": play, query_play, get_viewport_screenshot. "import_settings": import_assets, settings, save_assets, reload_assets, asset_editor, export_assets.

tools.name: play
tools.description: Playtest in Play In Editor as a human tester would, without execute_python: start (paused: true recommended: the game advances only during wait and input), stop, status, pause, resume, wait (game seconds and/or until a condition), input (Enhanced Input actions or keys), console, call (a function on a game actor), set (values, teleport). One call is one finished operation; results carry the session state and the errors, warnings and Print String lines logged meanwhile. Only the running game changes. Read it with query_play. Fields and errors: get_level_editing_guide topic "playtest" (read it first).

action.description: poll (with id): a result still pending. reset_input_settings: delete the saved Enhanced Input user settings.

console.description: start: a command or an array, run before the first frame.

until.description: wait: a condition or an array (any ends the wait).

tools.name: query_play
tools.description: Read the running Play In Editor game (read-only). what actors (default): filter by class, name, tag, near, or name actors ("player", "controller", "game_mode", a name, label or editor path); each with location, velocity, controller, vitals, playing montage, AI state and the values named in properties. what effects: active Niagara / Cascade components. what audio: playing audio components and the sounds started (since a seq). what log: the session's log, since a seq, by category, verbosity, text. what input: the player's active mapping contexts, effective keys and saved user settings. Refused without a session (Play.NoSession), except the log. Fields: get_level_editing_guide topic "playtest".

tools.name: execute_python
tools.description: Run Python in the editor, only for what no tool covers. Do not use it for saving, reloading, editor windows, exporting or level edits: those have their own tools (save_assets, reload_assets, asset_editor, export_assets; query_level and edit_level for the level). One transaction: on success one Edit > Undo entry titled by description (undo_title / undo_id for undo_editor); if it raises, what it recorded is undone (rolled_back: true, rolled_back_objects), earlier entries untouched. Work Undo cannot take back (assets created, renamed, deleted or saved, a map opened) is listed in not_undoable; a raising script that did such work is kept (rollback: "Kept", rollback_note). Only a code that is exactly one .py file path (optionally with arguments) runs that file.

tools.name: get_viewport_screenshot
tools.description: Capture an image: during Play In Editor the game as the player sees it, otherwise (or view "editor") the active Level Editor viewport. Default a JPEG of quality 70, at most 1024 px wide.

hud.description: Game view: include UMG widgets (default true).

max_width.description: Scaled down to this width (64-3840, default 1024).

tools.name: delete_assets
tools.description: Delete assets as the editor's Delete Assets dialog does (never forced); references among the assets of one call do not block. Result: {success, total, succeeded, failed, results[{asset, status, error?, referencers?[{kind: package|object|subobject, referencer, properties?}], undo_cleared?}]}. A failed asset makes it a tool error: referencers name what still uses it from outside the call (a referencer with refused_in_batch: true was in the call but refused itself). When only the editor's Undo history referenced an asset, the history is cleared (undo_cleared).

tools.name: import_assets
tools.description: Import local source files as the Content Browser's Import does, without dialogs: meshes (.fbx, .gltf/.glb, .obj), textures (.png, .jpg, .tga, .exr, ...) and sounds (.wav), with the project's default import settings; or reimport assets (action reimport), or list a file's import settings (action options). Only files the user named, as absolute paths. Options, results and errors: get_level_editing_guide topic "import_settings".

name.description: Asset name for a single file.

options.description: Common dialog settings (skeleton, mesh_type, collision, uniform_scale, srgb, compression, ...).

pipeline.description: Any other dialog setting by property name, nested by sub-pipeline.

tools.name: settings
tools.description: Read or write editor settings: section "world" is the open level's World Settings panel (a write is one Undo entry; the map stays dirty unless save: true); other sections are Project Settings sections, written to their default config file in the project (e.g. Config/DefaultEngine.ini), never to engine, plugin or user config. action list lists sections. Refused during Play In Editor. Guide: get_level_editing_guide topic "import_settings".

section.description: "world", or a display name ("Maps & Modes"), Category/Section or settings class.

properties.description: read: names (world without names: what differs from the defaults); write: {name: value} in AssetDocument value forms.

diff_only.description: read: only values that differ from the defaults.

description.description: world write: the Undo entry title.

dry_run.description: write: check and return the planned changes only.

tools.name: save_assets
tools.description: File > Save for assets, without dialogs: those with unsaved changes are saved, clean ones are listed in clean (force: true re-saves them). all_dirty: true is Save All (only: maps or content). Result: {saved[], clean[], not_saved[], refused[]}. Refused during Play In Editor.

tools.name: reload_assets
tools.description: Asset Actions > Reload: replace assets in memory with their files on disk, without dialogs. Unsaved changes are refused (Assets.UnsavedChanges) unless force: true discards them; assets of the open map are refused (Assets.OpenMap). Result: {reloaded[], not_loaded[], refused[]}. Refused during Play In Editor.

tools.name: asset_editor
tools.description: Open or close the editor window of assets (as double-clicking them in the Content Browser, or closing their tab), or list the assets that have one open. A document profile whose guide says so refuses an asset while its editor is open; close it first. An editor holding edits not yet applied to its asset (Material, Niagara: its Apply button is enabled) asks before closing: close refuses it (Assets.EditorNotClosed) unless discard_unapplied: true drops them; apply_editor presses the editor's Apply instead (the asset then has unsaved changes: save_assets, then extract it again). Result: {opened[] | closed[] (discarded_unapplied[]) | applied[], not_open[], open[]}; Assets.EditorNotOpened when the editor opened none.

assets.description: open / close / apply_editor: package or object paths.

discard_unapplied.description: close: close without the editor's unapplied edits (its close prompt's No).

tools.name: export_assets
tools.description: Asset Actions > Export, without dialogs: writes <folder>/<AssetName>.<format> per asset (default wav for sounds, png for textures; Assets.NoExporter lists the formats of other classes). folder: inside the project (default Saved/Exports). Existing files need overwrite: true. Result: {folder, exported[{asset, file, exporter, bytes}], refused[]}.
